content:
Requirement R14 (input): Input Sensor Move. Fixed modalities: Wearable/HMD and Touch. Intent: Allow the pilot to move/aim the UAV's sensor..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-14.1, F-14.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-14.<F>.1, Be-14.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-14.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R14 lets the pilot aim/reposition the UAV's ISR sensor toward a Point/Area of Interest, using Wearable/HMD and Touch as the fixed modalities (covers use case 6.2, "Move Sensor to POI/AOI").

**Function candidates:**

**F-14.1 — Point-designate a sensor target.**
The function is to let the pilot *designate a discrete location* (POI/AOI) that the sensor should slew to and hold. Goal: convert a pilot-chosen point in the world/on a display into a sensor aim-point. Effect measured by designation accuracy and slew-to-target success.

**F-14.2 — Continuously steer/aim the sensor.**
The function is to let the pilot *directly drive the sensor line-of-sight* in a closed loop — pan/tilt the sensor by continuous input rather than committing a single target. Goal: manual fine-aiming and exploratory scanning. Effect measured by tracking latency and aiming precision under continuous control.

**F-14.3 — Cue sensor from gaze/head vector.**
The function is to let the pilot aim the sensor by *where they are looking/facing* — the HMD head/eye vector becomes the sensor pointing command. Goal: hands-minimal, attention-coupled sensor cueing when hands are on flight controls. Effect measured by cue-to-slew accuracy and hands-free completion.

These are genuinely distinct goals: F-14.1 is discrete commit-a-point, F-14.2 is continuous manual drive, F-14.3 is attention/gaze-coupled cueing. Note F-14.3 leans heavily on HMD-as-input and could later share behaviour with any other "look-to-designate" requirement.

Which function do you want to close on?

Can't close on all three — the requirement resolves to one closed F index so Behaviour/Structure labels stay tractable. But these three aren't really competing goals; they're complementary aiming modes. Two ways to handle it:

**Option A — Pick one primary.** Given the fixed modalities (HMD + Touch) and the cockpit constraints (hands often on HOTAS, high workload), **F-14.3 (gaze/head-vector cue)** is the strongest fit for HMD, and **F-14.1 (point-designate)** is the strongest fit for Touch. F-14.2 (continuous manual drive) fits neither fixed modality cleanly — continuous pan/tilt wants a rate device (TDC/HOTAS), not Touch or HMD, so it's the weakest of the three for R14's modality pair.

**Option B — Fold into one function.** Define a single function "designate a sensor aim-point," where head/gaze (HMD) and touch-on-map (Touch) are two *input pathways* to the same goal — that's exactly the Behaviour layer's job (one pathway per modality). F-14.2's continuous-drive goal is genuinely different and would be dropped or spun into its own requirement.

My recommendation: **close on the folded function (Option B)** — it captures F-14.1 and F-14.3 as one coherent goal ("aim the sensor at a pilot-designated point") realized by two modality pathways, and defers F-14.2's continuous-steering as out-of-scope for this modality pair.

Proposed closed function:

**F-14 — Designate a sensor aim-point.** Convert a pilot-chosen POI/AOI (via head/gaze or via touch) into a sensor slew-and-hold command. Measured by designation accuracy and slew-to-target success.

Want me to close on this folded F-14, or keep F-14.1 and F-14.3 as separate closed indices (which means running Behaviour/Structure twice)?

**Function closed: F-14 — Designate a sensor aim-point.** Convert a pilot-chosen POI/AOI (via head/gaze or via touch) into a sensor slew-and-hold command. F-14.2 (continuous manual steering) deferred as out-of-scope for this modality pair.

---

**Behaviour candidates** (one per fixed-modality pathway, plus Mixed):

**Be-14.1 — Touch-only (touch-on-map designate).**
Pilot taps the POI, or drags a box for an AOI, directly on the WAD Map view. A designation marker drops at the tapped point; the pilot confirms and the system issues the slew command. Long-press or second-tap arms the confirm. Full task completable on Touch alone (tap → confirm → sensor slews → ack shown in-pane). Precision aided by drag-to-refine before confirm.

**Be-14.2 — HMD-only (head/gaze designate).**
Pilot's HMD reticle (head-vector, eye-tracked refinement) sits on the target in the visor overlay; a dwell or a discrete confirm freezes the designation and issues the slew. Sensor aim-point set by where the pilot is looking. Full task completable HMD-alone: aim reticle → confirm-by-dwell → slew → in-visor ack. Strong when hands are on HOTAS.

**Be-14.3 — Mixed (gaze-to-coarse, touch-to-refine-and-commit).**
HMD head/gaze does the coarse cue (fast, gets the reticle in the neighborhood), then Touch on WAD refines the exact point and commits the confirm. Adds real value: gaze is fast but coarse/jittery, touch is precise but slow to traverse the display — combining them beats either alone for accuracy-under-time. This is the pathway that best exploits *both* fixed modalities.

Per the redundancy rule, Be-14.1 and Be-14.2 must each be independently sufficient; Be-14.3 is an efficiency path, not a required one.

Note: Be-14.2's HMD gaze-designate mechanism is a strong reuse candidate for any future "look-to-designate/track" requirement (e.g. R7 UAV tracking target ID) — flag for consolidation later.

Which behaviour(s) to carry into Structure?

All three carry forward — they're the three required pathways (Touch-alone, HMD-alone, Mixed), so each needs its structural realization. Structures below; several elements are shared across pathways (that's expected — the redundancy rule wants common surfaces, not three separate stovepipes).

---

**For Be-14.1 (Touch-only):**

**S-14.1.1 — Map-embedded designation, in-context.**
On WAD Map view: tap-to-drop POI marker / drag-box for AOI, a **SENSOR AIM** designation layer (overlay) showing the pending marker, a bezel/Touch **CONFIRM SLEW** button, and an in-pane slew-progress + ack indicator (reuses R12 status-pane ack pattern). Everything happens on the existing Map — no new window.

**S-14.1.2 — Dedicated Sensor-Control overlay panel.**
A separate stacked WAD overlay (a "SENSOR" panel, sibling to R11 UAV PARAMS) with its own mini-map/feed thumbnail, coordinate readout of the tapped point, and a confirm gate. Designation still by touch, but isolated from the main Map layer. Cleaner state ownership, costs a panel slot.

---

**For Be-14.2 (HMD-only):**

**S-14.2.1 — In-visor reticle + dwell-confirm.**
HMD overlay renders a head-slaved aiming reticle with eye-tracked fine offset, a dwell-timer ring as the confirm affordance, and an in-visor slew/ack cue. No WAD interaction needed — completable heads-out.

**S-14.2.2 — In-visor reticle + discrete-confirm (bezel OSS / Touch tap).**
Same in-visor reticle, but commit is a discrete press (bezel OSS or single WAD tap) instead of dwell — avoids dwell false-commits and Midas-touch problems. Note: this borrows a Touch/bezel element for confirm, so it's not *strictly* HMD-only for the commit step. Given the redundancy rule (HMD must be independently sufficient), **S-14.2.1 is the compliant HMD-alone structure**; S-14.2.2 is really a Mixed variant.

---

**For Be-14.3 (Mixed):**

**S-14.3.1 — Gaze-cue + touch-refine, shared confirm gate.**
Reuses S-14.2.1's in-visor reticle for coarse cueing and S-14.1.1's Map designation layer for refine + commit. The reticle's coarse point seeds the WAD marker; pilot nudges it by touch/TDC and confirms via the shared **CONFIRM SLEW** gate. Maximal reuse — no new elements, just a data handoff (gaze vector → marker seed).

**S-14.3.2 — Gaze-cue + bezel-step commit.**
In-visor reticle for coarse aim, bezel rotary to step-refine the aim-point, bezel OSS to commit. Keeps hands near throttle/bezel rather than reaching to WAD. Useful under vibration/turbulence when precise touch is hard.

---

**My recommendation:** close on **S-14.1.1** (Touch), **S-14.2.1** (HMD-alone, redundancy-compliant), and **S-14.3.1** (Mixed, maximal reuse). This gives one coherent designation model — a shared Map designation layer + shared CONFIRM SLEW gate + in-visor reticle — realizing all three pathways without duplicating structure.

Shared/reuse flags: the CONFIRM SLEW gate follows the R09/R10 dual-input confirm pattern; the ack indicator reuses R12; the in-visor reticle (S-14.2.1) is the reuse anchor for future look-to-designate requirements.

Which structures do you want to close on?

Closing on those two, with one flag you should register:

**S-14.2.2 breaks the HMD-alone redundancy rule for Be-14.2.** Its commit is a bezel-OSS / WAD-tap press, so the HMD pathway is no longer independently sufficient — the pilot cannot complete the task on HMD alone. That's fine *if* you accept that R14's redundancy is satisfied at the requirement level (Touch-alone via S-14.1.1 is fully sufficient; HMD contributes designation but leans on a discrete confirm), rather than each pathway being self-complete. Given the Midas-touch / false-dwell risk you're implicitly avoiding by picking S-14.2.2, that's a defensible trade — but it means **F-14 is not HMD-modality-complete**; it's Touch-complete with an HMD-assisted path.

If you want strict HMD-alone completeness you'd need S-14.2.1 (dwell-confirm) instead or in addition. Your call — I'll record it as chosen with the caveat noted.

**Final structures for R14:**

- **S-14.1.1 — Map-embedded designation (Touch path):** WAD Map view with tap-to-drop POI / drag-box AOI, a SENSOR AIM designation overlay layer, a Touch/bezel CONFIRM SLEW gate (R09/R10 confirm pattern), and in-pane slew-progress + ack (R12 pattern). Independently sufficient — carries the requirement's modality-completeness.

- **S-14.2.2 — In-visor reticle + discrete-confirm (HMD-assisted path):** HMD head-slaved reticle with eye-tracked fine offset and in-visor slew/ack cue; commit via bezel OSS or single WAD tap. Not HMD-alone-complete (commit borrows Touch/bezel) — recorded as an accepted deviation from strict per-pathway redundancy.

Reuse flags: CONFIRM SLEW gate ← R09/R10; ack indicator ← R12; the in-visor reticle is the reuse anchor for future look-to-designate requirements (e.g. R7 tracking target ID).

R14 is fully specified across all three layers (F-14 → Be-14.1/.2/.3 → S-14.1.1, S-14.2.2). Ready to close R14, or revisit the redundancy caveat?
It's fine if F-14's HMD is not modality complete.

Recorded. R14 closed.

**R14 — Input Sensor Move — final:**

- **F-14 — Designate a sensor aim-point.** Convert a pilot-chosen POI/AOI (via head/gaze or touch) into a sensor slew-and-hold command. Continuous manual steering (former F-14.2) deferred out-of-scope for this modality pair.

- **Be-14.1 (Touch)** → **S-14.1.1** — Map-embedded designation: WAD Map tap-to-drop POI / drag-box AOI, SENSOR AIM overlay layer, Touch/bezel CONFIRM SLEW gate (R09/R10 pattern), in-pane slew-progress + ack (R12 pattern). *Independently sufficient — carries requirement-level modality completeness.*

- **Be-14.2 (HMD)** → **S-14.2.2** — In-visor head-slaved reticle with eye-tracked fine offset + in-visor slew/ack cue; commit via bezel OSS or single WAD tap. *HMD-assisted, not HMD-alone-complete — accepted deviation from strict per-pathway redundancy (confirmed by designer).*

- **Be-14.3 (Mixed)** — carried as the gaze-cue + touch-refine efficiency path; realized by the combination of the two structures above (reticle coarse-cue seeds the Map marker, touch refines and commits). No dedicated structure.

**Reuse flags for consolidation:** CONFIRM SLEW gate ← R09/R10; ack indicator ← R12; in-visor reticle is the reuse anchor for future look-to-designate/track requirements (notably R7 UAV tracking target ID).

Ready for R15.
